body:
Two input mistakes in run `a348af56b1f15298` (task:1ba2b996f1282bbb) cost turns because the reply didn't say what was wrong:

- `view rust_submit.Store::resolve_module 2>/dev/null || true` replied E1001 unknown name, quoting the whole line, so the agent kept writing shell suffixes.
- A patch sent in `command` instead of `text` replied "needs the new code in the `text` argument" and listed 102 skipped lines (every patch line read as a command).

1. A command line containing a shell redirect, pipe or `||`/`&&` (outside quotes) is refused before running, once: "commands are not shell: drop `2>/dev/null || true`" (naming the part found).
2. When `command` holds a line starting `*** Begin Patch`, refuse the whole call with "the patch goes in `text`; `command` is just `submit`" and don't list the patch lines as skipped.
3. Both are language-neutral.
4. Tests: each refusal's wording; a quoted `|` in `grep` or `find` text still runs.

Checks: `rust-unit`, `rust-acceptance`.

Left out: running the command anyway with the suffix stripped (it would hide the mistake from the agent and from review).
title: hints: shell syntax and patches in command
